concerns.text: Phase 6 (T040-T043) implements 'Scaling Law & Computational Irreducibility Analysis' to address reviewer concerns (West, Wolfram, Dyson). These tasks have no corresponding Functional Requirement (FR) or Success Criterion (SC) in spec.md. The spec explicitly limits scope to 3 cycles and specific metrics (FR-007, SC-003). Implementing unrequested philosophical safeguards constitutes scope creep and violates the constraint that tasks must not introduce unapproved scope.

spec.md FR-004 mandates a fixed batch size of 4. Tasks T032 and T032b implement 'dynamic batch size reduction' (halving if RAM > 6.5GB) and 'auto-scaling'. While necessary for hardware constraints, this silently relaxes the explicit FR-004 requirement without a documented exception or parameter override mechanism in the spec. A task that changes a fixed hyperparameter mandated by an FR is a constraint violation unless the spec explicitly allows staging or dynamic adjustment.

Task T041 implements 'Kolmogorov complexity (approximated via Lempel-Ziv compression)' to address Wolfram's concerns. spec.md SC-003 only requires fitting an exponential decay model to identify plateau/degradation. The complexity metric is an unrequested addition that does not map to any measurable success criterion, violating the principle that tasks must not silently relax or expand requirements beyond the spec's defined acceptance criteria.

spec.md Edge Cases mandate 'Fail-Fast' for missing data files. Task T005a correctly implements this. However, Task T004 (memory watchdog) and T032 (dynamic batch size) introduce 'graceful degradation' (reducing batch size) for RAM constraints, whereas the spec's Edge Cases for dataset availability are strict fail-fast. The tasks mix strict fail-fast (data) with graceful degradation (RAM) without explicitly distinguishing these in the spec's Edge Cases, potentially violating the 'no silent constitution drift' principle if the RAM handling is interpreted as a relaxation of the strict execution constraints implied by the 7GB limit.
